name: Fighter A (placeholder)
notes: PLACEHOLDER IDENTITY. The character id is the file stem, fighter_a; the display name says placeholder in so many words; every move id is generic and descriptive. Nothing here carries a theme, a personality or a piece of flavour text, because the roster is not named yet and a name authored now is a rename later. This is the FIRST ORIGINAL CHARACTER in the project: the three in tests/fixtures/characters are transcribed from third-party MUGEN characters this project holds no licence to, and they are evidence, not content.

AUTHORED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. There is no .cns behind this file, so no [P] field carries a file:line and every engine.derivation says AUTHORED in capitals and names the design rule instead. That is the honest form of assertion A12 for an original character. It also changes what the fit measurement means: 0 of 18 moves need an escape hatch, against ADR-001's 23 of 59, and the reason is not that this character is simpler -- it is that it was authored against schema v2 rather than pushed into schema v1.

STAGE IS CORNER, and that is the question this file is designed to answer. comboprover.hpp is corner-only by construction (:15-24), so the corner verdict is the one the editor computes live and the one the ranking certificate belongs to. walk_speed and every pushback are authored and real, but at stage corner model.py drops horizontal position entirely, so this character's verdict does NOT rest on the pushback number that ADR-001:386-404 shows flips Kung Fu Girl's midscreen verdict at a 20% error.

LAW 1, and it is the whole ground game: every GROUND move in this file is at most +2 on hit, and the fastest move in the file is 3 frames. Therefore no ground move links into any ground move, and every combo edge this character has is a cancel that appears in the cancels array. THE CANCEL TABLE IS COMPLETE. That is the property the three transcribed characters lack: a +4 or +5 light with 3f startup has a link edge that no .cmd table lists, and ADR-001:420-432 reports exactly that edge as the corner infinite in two of the three.

LAW 2: TWO moves break Law 1 on purpose and both are aerials at +7 on hit -- air_mp, and air_hp since the 6/6/6 pass -- and all nine of the link edges each one's frame data implies are authored rather than omitted. Both are safe because of Law 3. THE OTHER FOUR AERIALS ARE +2 AND IMPLY NOTHING, which is the reason six air moves cost this character eighteen descending edges rather than fifty: an aerial is exempt from Law 1 only if its frame data actually claims the advantage, and four of the six decline to.

LAW 3: juggle is spent, never gained, and every edge whose TARGET is an air move spends it. Every cycle in the usable cancel graph must pass through such an edge, so every cycle strictly decreases juggle. This is the termination argument, and engine.termination_argument states it as a checkable claim rather than a hope. THE 6/6/6 PASS TRIPLED THE AIR ROSTER AND DID NOT TOUCH THE LAW: there are now six air moves and fifteen edges entering one, against two and four before, and the law is unchanged because it was never a statement about how many aerials there are. Every one of the four new aerials carries a negative effect.juggle, and a single one that did not would have been a free route around the whole argument.

METER GAIN IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM [P] effect, and this is the file's one significant modelling decision. The character does build meter on hit -- engine.reaction.meter_gain_units carries the real numbers on all 18 moves -- but a POSITIVE entry in [P] effect clears comboprover.hpp:376-386's spendOnly flag and destroys the ranking certificate (:563), which is why ADR-001 gate 3 measured hasRanking false on every real character. The omission UNDER-credits the attacker's meter, which is the direction that can HIDE an infinite, so it is justified rather than waved at: see engine.termination_argument.meter_is_not_load_bearing, which states the structural reason and names the counterfactual that checks it.

Juggle RESET is not modelled, and that is EXACT rather than a loss. The reset happens when the combo ends and the defender lands, which is outside the cancel graph by construction. Within one combo juggle only ever decreases, so the model is not approximating anything here. This is the first file in the project in which the juggle half of the resource vocabulary carries data at all: ADR-001:519-521 records that juggle is dead data in all three Phase-0 characters and that half of the vocabulary is therefore untested.

decay is `none`, and none is the WORST CASE for termination rather than a gap. Any decay only lowers hitstun, which only lowers advantage, which only removes edges from outgoing[] (comboprover.hpp:338-348) and only adds distinctions to the hits component of a configuration. Both effects make a loop harder to close, so a TERMINATING verdict at `none` implies TERMINATING under every decay rule schema v2 can express. Proving it at the worst case is why this character does not need a decay rule to be finite.

Resource order is [meter, juggle], the build-wide contract of assertion A03. Both resources carry data here, which is new: comboprover::Character keys a ResourceVec positionally (:56, :128-129, :152), so a file that declared them in the other order would silently compare this character's juggle budget against another character's meter.

engine.derivation: AUTHORED as none. A01 holds with room: floor 0 against a smallest authored hitstun of 12 (stand_lp and crouch_lp). A02 holds: multiplicative is not used and is no longer a legal kind.
engine.why_none_rather_than_a_house_rule: Two reasons, and the second is the one that decides it. (1) SOUNDNESS: none is the worst case, so the verdict proved here holds under any decay the schema can express -- see notes[]. (2) MEASUREMENT: both implementations evaluate every edge at the SETTLED hitstun (comboprover.hpp:338-339), so linear decay does not soften this character's cancel table, it deletes it. Authoring linear step 2 floor 10 was measured twice, and the two files answer differently: the old two-aerial file lost 46 of its 73 edges AND the certificate (zero resource-spending edges survived, anyDown false); this six-aerial roster (remeasured 2026-08-31, tests/test_variants.cpp `decay_linear`) keeps 35 of 94 edges and the certificate SURVIVES -- while the verdict's stated worst case collapses to 5 hits, BELOW the 7 the kernel demonstrably performs, because the kernel carries no decay at all. That is a sharper form of ADR-001's D8 finding than either loss: inventing a decay rule by eye can leave the proof standing over the wrong game.
engine.if_a_decay_rule_is_ever_wanted: Author it as `table` with integer permille multipliers, which is D8's preferred escape, and re-measure the certificate and not just the verdict. Do not reach for `linear` by eye.

engine.derivation: 1 unit = 1/100 bar, the build-wide unit ADR-001 section 3 gate 2 fixes at 10 MUGEN power. This character is not a MUGEN import so nothing needs to divide evenly, but the unit is inherited unchanged so that fighter_a and the three fixtures can be compared without a conversion.
engine.why_initial_is_the_ceiling: 300 is deliberately the maximum, not a typical starting value. The model never GAINS meter (see notes[]), so starting anywhere below the ceiling would under-credit the attacker twice over. Starting AT the ceiling over-credits the opening state, which is the permissive direction ADR-001:224-225 calls safe: it can invent a combo the character could not afford, it cannot hide one.
engine.ceiling_warning: comboprover.hpp carries no ceiling at all (Character :148-174, nonNegative :264-269 hardcodes floor 0) while model.py:192 clamps. The adapter must clamp in its own search loop (ADR-001 section 8 item 4). This character never gains meter, so nothing in it can reach the ceiling from below and the divergence is inert here -- but it is inert by accident of this file, not fixed.

engine.derivation: AUTHORED. 4 points per combo. ALL SIX AIR MOVES SPEND IT and nothing anywhere returns a point: the four air lights and mediums cost 1 each (air_lp, air_lk, air_mp, air_mk) and the two air heavies cost 2 (air_hp, air_hk), on the tier rule air_hk's note has always stated -- the heavy juggle costs double. THE BUDGET WAS NOT RAISED WHEN THE ROSTER TRIPLED, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. 4 is exactly the price of the longest ascending air string the character can perform -- a light (1), a medium (1) and a heavy ender (2) -- so the budget buys one complete string and no more. It also still buys air_mp x4, or air_mp x2 then air_hk, and still never air_mp x3 then air_hk. Opening with the heavy jump-in air_hp spends 2 of the 4 before the combo starts, which leaves a light and a medium but no heavy ender: that trade is the point of the move costing what it costs.
engine.semantics: A PER-COMBO budget, not a per-launch one, because the prover asks about a single unbounded combo and has no combo-reset event. The reset is real and happens when the defender lands; it is outside the cancel graph by construction, so modelling juggle as monotone within a combo is EXACT and not an approximation. The budget SIZE is not what makes the character finite -- setting initial to 0 or to 40 leaves the verdict and the certificate unchanged -- the MONOTONE DECREASE is.
engine.why_this_is_the_first_file_with_live_jug: ADR-001:519-521 records that juggle is dead data in all three Phase-0 characters: Kung Fu Girl disables MUGEN's juggle system outright, Kung Fu Man does not use it, and AOF2 has none, so 'the juggle half of the resource vocabulary is entirely untested by Phase 0'. This file is the test.

engine.derivation: AUTHORED. An 18-tick forward dash covering 56 px, which is one space unit per pixel at model.py:465-468's scale of 100 against a 100 px reach unit. engine.inert_at_this_stage: stage is corner, where model.py:453-456 drops horizontal position, so __space does not exist and this action is a pure frame cost with no effect -- it can never help the attacker and can never create an edge. A jump is not a cancel, so there is no edge to author; [P] starters is empty, which comboprover.hpp:350-353 reads as `every move is a starter`, so the move is reachable and its nine landing links are live. engine.schema_version_note: RAISED FROM 2 TO 3 BY THE ANNOTATION PASS engine.stance_and_guard describes, and unlike v2's equivalent line this one carries information. Nothing in code keys off it -- CharacterData.cpp does not read it at all -- so it is a claim the author makes about themselves, and the claim is specific: this file has CONSIDERED stance precision and block height on every move, as opposed to simply not having either. That distinction is the only thing separating a v3 file from a v2 one that happens to validate. THE DOCUMENT IS STILL AT Editor/src/Exported/Characters/schema.v2.json: a JSON Schema's identity is its $id (character.v3.json), nothing in this repository resolves it by path, and the file's own first key says so.

assets.id_note: The character id is the FILE STEM. Schema v2 sets additionalProperties false at the top level and declares no `id` key, and json_spec.py:205-207 substitutes the file stem when `name` is absent, so fighter_a.json IS the id. It is recorded here as well so a reader does not have to infer it from a filename.
assets.naming_policy: NEUTRAL PLACEHOLDER, held deliberately. Move ids are generic and descriptive (stand_lp, crouch_mk, special_fireball, super_beam) so that naming the roster later is a display-string change and never a data migration. No move id, label or note in this file carries a theme.

constants.source: AUTHORED. Every distance is an exact integer number of sub-units at 256 per pixel: walk 3 px/tick = 768, gravity 0.5 px/tick^2 = 128, jump 11 px/tick = 2816. ADR-001:499-504 records that Kung Fu Man's 2.4 px/tick walk CANNOT be expressed as (integer px)/100 and loses 0.4 px/tick through model.py:468's int(round(v*100)). This character's 3 px/tick is 0.03 reach units and survives that quantization exactly, because an original character can choose numbers that quantize and this one does everywhere.

quantized_sources.note: reach_px, pushback_px and damage_hundredths are carried per move rather than in one table here: reach_px is move.reach * 100, pushback_px is move.pushback * 100, damage_hundredths is move.damage * 100, and every one of the three is an exact integer by construction because the [P] float was DERIVED FROM the integer rather than the other way round. That inversion is the point of D8 and it is the reason no value in this file needs a rounding rule.

engine.derivation_legend: Every move's engine.derivation reads: what shape the move is, then the arithmetic behind any number a reader would otherwise have to trust. There are no file:line citations anywhere in this file and their absence is correct, not an omission: this character is authored, so its provenance is a design rule, and assertion A12's 'name a file:line or say ESTIMATED in capitals' is satisfied here by AUTHORED in capitals plus the rule. Nothing in this file is ESTIMATED. ADR-001:486-497 names pushback and hitstun decay as the two quantities Phase 0 could only estimate; this character has neither problem, because it defines its own pushback displacement and has no decay.

derivation_defaults.startup: The first tick on which the move can connect: a hit box exists AND the hit is registered. Tick 1 is the first tick of the state.
derivation_defaults.recovery: Total state length - startup - active, except for the SEVEN moves whose state ends on a landing predicate -- all six aerials and special_uppercut -- where it is a LOWER bound and engine.transitions[].duration_bound says so. It was three before the 6/6/6 pass; every aerial added by that pass ends on the same predicate for the same reason, so the count tracks the air roster and always will.
derivation_defaults.hitstun: Ticks the defender is frozen, before decay. For super_beam it is hits[0]'s, per assertion A05.
derivation_defaults.damage: [P] float = engine damage_hundredths / 100. For super_beam it is the SUM over hits[], which json_spec.py:69 sends to Result.maxDamage only.
derivation_defaults.reach: Clsn1 extent in pixels / 100, plus any forward travel the move drives itself through, because reach is an upper bound on the GAP (model.py:473-476) and a move that travels can close a gap the box alone cannot.
derivation_defaults.pushback: |pushback velocity px/tick| * slide ticks / 2, the same rule Phase 0 applied to all three fixtures -- but DERIVED here rather than estimated, because this character chooses the velocity and the slide time.
derivation_defaults.effect_and_guard: Only two resources exist and neither is ever gained. See termination_argument.
derivation_defaults.stance_and_blocked_as: Both are per move and both are stated on all eighteen; the rule that assigned them is engine.stance_and_guard and each move's engine.stance_and_guard_note carries its own argument.

stance_and_guard.what_this_pass_did: Annotated all eighteen existing moves against schema v3 and added none, removed none, and changed no frame number, no cancel, no delay and no resource effect. Four fields: [P] move.stance replaced with a precise value, [G] move.blocked_as on every move, engine.hurtbox_sub on three, engine.airborne_from_tick on one. THIS PASS TOUCHES EXACTLY ONE PROVER-VISIBLE FIELD -- move.stance -- and only by replacing `ground` with a more precise value drawn from the same closed vocabulary. Nothing else it writes is readable by json_spec.py, by comboprover.hpp or by cse::kernel.
stance_and_guard.where_the_data_came_from_because_none_of: THE CHARACTER ALREADY KNEW ALL OF THIS AND HAD NOWHERE TO PUT IT, which is ADR-006 section 9's finding restated on this file. STANCE was in engine.tags as `stand` / `crouch` / `air`, on all fourteen normals, since the day the file was written. GUARD HEIGHT was in engine.tags as `low` on exactly three moves -- crouch_lk, crouch_mk, crouch_hk -- and again in [P] label as the English `(low)` and `(sweep, knockdown)`. So the three lows below are not a judgement made now: they are this file's own claim promoted from a free string an id-reading heuristic would have had to guess at, into a field a loader reads. The tags are left exactly where they are, as provenance. THE ONLY FOUR MOVES THAT NEEDED DECIDING are the four with no stance tag -- the three specials and the super -- and one of those four decided itself: special_fireball's stance is read off engine.projectile.offset_sub.y, a number the file already carried.

the_blocked_as_table.low: crouch_lk, crouch_mk, crouch_hk. Exactly the three the file already tagged `low`, and exactly the three ADR-006 section 1.5 lists as declaring their guard height in a display string.
the_blocked_as_table.high: ALL SIX AERIALS and nothing else -- air_lp, air_lk, air_mp, air_mk, air_hp, air_hk, four of them added by the later 6/6/6 pass. This character has NO overhead on the ground -- no standing or crouching move is `high` -- which is a real statement about it rather than an omission, and one that no file could make before v3. WHAT CHANGED WHEN THE ROSTER TRIPLED IS NOT THE RULE BUT ITS WEIGHT: `high` on a committed 6f or 8f jump-in describes geometry, and `high` on a 4f air-to-air jab is a mixup -- the fastest attack in the file a crouching block does not stop. Same value, two different claims, and moves[air_lp].engine.stance_and_guard_note is where the second one is argued.
the_blocked_as_table.mid: the other thirteen. MID IS THE DECISION AND NOT MERELY THE DEFAULT, and the schema is honest that a default cannot tell those two apart (x-migration: `there is no way to tell a move that was considered and is a mid from one nobody thought about`). That is what the per-move notes are for. Three of the thirteen had to be argued rather than assumed: crouch_lp and crouch_mp, crouching and not low, on ADR-006 section 2's `a sweep and a crouching jab are both crouching and only one is low`; and crouch_hp, the anti-air launcher, which is the counterexample the orthogonality of the two fields rests on and whose note is the longest in the file for that reason.

stance_and_guard.why_nothing_cross_checks_the_two: NOT AN OMISSION. Three checks were available and all three are refused by decision, in the schema (x-v3-changes.the_check_that_was_refused), in CharacterData.h's note on BlockHeight, and in ADR-006 section 10 item 3: warn when a `crouching` move is not `low`; warn when an `air` move is not `high`; warn when a `standing` move is `low`. Every one of them encodes the word USUALLY and every one of them fires on a move IN THIS FILE -- the first on crouch_hp, the second on nothing here but on most of Street Fighter, the third on the standing overhead this character does not happen to have. A diagnostic that fires on correct data is how a diagnostic gets deleted, and this project has already learned that once with assertion A04.
stance_and_guard.the_hurtbox_policy_and_why_three_moves_a: A BOX IS AUTHORED WHERE THE HEIGHT IS A DESIGN DECISION AND NOWHERE ELSE. Three moves carry one, all crouching: crouch_mk at 26 px, which ducks; crouch_hk at 20 px, the sweep, which ducks furthest and pays for it with a 48 px body; and crouch_hp at 36 px, which deliberately does NOT duck. THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS DEFENDING, because schema x-migration says to author a box `on crouching attacks that should low-profile, and only those`. It is here for two reasons. First, 36 px is what turns `this crouching attack does not duck` from a silence into a NUMBER, which is the author's `not every crouching attack would low profile` made arithmetic -- and a silence would have meant the standing 60 px body, which is not what a crouching anti-air is. Second, schema x-worked-examples.low_profile_is_a_shape already fixes this move's box at 9216, so authoring anything else, INCLUDING NOTHING, would put the schema and the character file into disagreement about one move of one character. THE OTHER THREE CROUCHING MOVES -- crouch_lp, crouch_mp, crouch_lk -- carry no override and therefore present the character's default 60 px body from engine.constants. That OVER-STATES how tall they are, which makes them easier to hit, which is the conservative direction, and which is the state all eighteen moves were in before this pass. It is not an omission awaiting a tidy-up: pasting one default body onto every move states nothing, and what this file is trying to say is which crouches are different from each other.
stance_and_guard.the_y_axis_trap_in_this_very_file: STATED ONCE HERE AND AGAIN ON EVERY BOX, because it is the one mistake A15 cannot refuse. engine.hurtbox_sub is +Y UP with the floor at 0, matching cse::kernel::Box and what MatchBuilder.cpp builds. engine.constants.default_pushbox_sub in this same file is [-3328, -15360, 3328, 0], which is MUGEN's Y-DOWN with the head at -60 px. THEY ARE THE SAME BODY WRITTEN TWO WAYS and both are well-formed rectangles of identical size, so A15's inversion, emptiness and range clauses all pass either one -- an author reaching for a hurtbox will reach for the pushbox already sitting in the file, and get a body sixty pixels underground that nothing but a warning will catch. All three boxes here author y0 = 0.
stance_and_guard.the_airborne_policy_and_why_one_move_and: ONE MOVE HAS ONE: special_uppercut, tick 3, DERIVED from engine.motion and engine.transitions rather than chosen -- its note carries the arithmetic and the A14 bound. NOTHING ELSE IN THE FILE EARNS ONE, and the file says so on the three moves where a reader would look rather than leaving it to be inferred from an absence. stand_hk and crouch_hp are launchers that launch the DEFENDER and end on frame transitions; special_dash_punch authors vel_y_sub 0 on every keyframe and gravity_sub 0; the two aerials were airborne before they began, where the schema says the field would say nothing new rather than something false. THERE IS NO HOP KICK IN THIS CHARACTER, and that is why the hop-over half of the mechanism is expressible here and not exercised here. The author's own example of it -- Ryu's f+HK -- is a COMMAND NORMAL, and command normals are scoped out by ADR-006 section 8 and blocked on a most-specific-wins rule in StepAttack rather than on any field. Inventing a hop kick to exercise the field would have meant ADDING A MOVE, which this pass does not do.
stance_and_guard.the_census_A16_now_sees: standing 10, crouching 6, air 6, `ground` 0, AND A16 NOW WARNS ABOUT NOTHING. The annotation pass left exactly one warning standing -- air, 2 of 6 -- and called it `the shortest complete description of what this character is missing: four aerials`. The 6/6/6 pass added those four and the warning went out. THAT IS THE ASSERTION DOING ITS JOB END TO END and it is worth recording as such: A16 was authored to name a shortfall on real data, it named one, the shortfall was filled, and the diagnostic went quiet without anybody editing the diagnostic. READ THE STANDING FIGURE CAREFULLY, because it is the one line that still diverges: it is 10 because A16 counts BY STANCE, and the three specials and the super are standing too, while the 6/6/6 convention counts NORMALS and this character has exactly six standing normals. ADR-006 section 8's table says 6 for that reason and A16 says 10 for the other; schema x-load-assertions.A16 records the divergence deliberately rather than leaving somebody to find it as a bug, and closing it needs a move CATEGORY field, which is a v4 conversation. The air line is now 6 by BOTH counts, because all six aerials are normals.
stance_and_guard.cannot_move_a_measured_number: STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN MEASURED-AND-HOPED, which matters because this file's verdict, its cycle count, its usable-dead split and its ranking certificate are all asserted by tests. READ THIS AS A CLAIM ABOUT THE ANNOTATION PASS ONLY. It was true and it held: annotating stance and blocked_as moved nothing. The LATER 6/6/6 pass moved all four numbers on purpose -- 41 cycles became 121 and 68/5 became 88/6 -- because it added four moves and twenty-one edges, which is a change to the CHARACTER rather than to its description. The two passes are separated here so that a future reader does not read this paragraph as a promise the file has since broken; see engine.the_six_six_six_pass. (1) THE PROVER HAS NO STANCE AND NO BLOCKING. comboprover.hpp contains no stance concept at all, and ProverAdapter.cpp never passes stance into comboprover::Character -- its single use is a projection loss count, `if (m.stance != Stance::Any) ++stanced`, and `standing` and `crouching` are != Any exactly as `ground` was, so even that count is unchanged at 18. Nothing in the fragment concerns blocking: model.py:81's COMBO_CONTACT counts `hit` and `always` and stops. (2) THE KERNEL CANNOT SEE ANY OF THE FOUR. cse::kernel::MoveDef carries startup, active, recovery, damage, hitstun, hitbox and button and nothing else, so the connect handshake's MatchData hash is byte-identical across this pass; MatchBuilder builds the body from kDefaultBodyHalfWidthSub and kDefaultBodyHeightSub and never from engine.hurtbox_sub. (3) THE THREE ENGINE FIELDS ARE INVISIBLE TO json_spec.py by the argument v2 already measured -- _move() reads thirteen named keys and enumerates none. ADR-006 section 10 item 9 makes this the regression test for the whole ADR: if any verdict moves, something was implemented wrongly.
stance_and_guard.the_one_thing_that_is_not_free: RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED, and it is the price of the only [P] change here. ADR-006 section 5 measures model.py:120-121 validating stance against a closed three-value tuple and RAISING, so this file authoring `standing` and `crouching` is UNLOADABLE by the unmodified reference implementation until that one line is widened to five. It costs THIS character nothing today: it declares stage `corner`, and the corner verdict is the C++ header's, which has no stance at all. It costs the MIDSCREEN path everything, because comboprover.hpp is corner-only by construction and Python is therefore the only midscreen path there is. ADR-006 section 10 item 7 is the remedy, it is one line, and it is provably verdict-neutral because no decision procedure in the reference reads the field. The three MUGEN fixtures keep authoring `ground` and are unaffected either way.

the_six_six_six_pass.what_it_did: Added the FOUR MISSING AERIALS -- air_lp, air_lk, air_mk, air_hp -- bringing the character to the author's standard of six standing normals, six crouching normals and six aerials. 18 moves became 22 and 73 cancel edges became 94. It changed NO existing move: not a frame number, not a resource effect, not a tag, not a note. It changed no existing cancel edge either, and in particular it added no edge OUT of air_mp, whose eleven outgoing edges are what the gap-extent measurement is built on. Everything it altered outside the two arrays is prose that had gone stale, listed in what_prose_it_corrected.
the_six_six_six_pass.the_six_roles: The character now reads as three pairs rather than two loose moves. AIR-TO-AIR LIGHTS (air_lp 4f, air_lk 5f): fast, cheap, +2 on hit so they convert into nothing on the ground, and they exist to open an air string. AIR MEDIUMS, one of each kind: air_mp is the jump-in that converts at +7 and air_mk is the air-to-air continuer at +2 that hands off to the ender. AIR HEAVIES, mirror images: air_hp OPENS a combo -- +7, nine landing links, and nothing cancels into it -- while air_hk ENDS one, knocks down, and nothing cancels out of it. TWO OF SIX CONVERT ON LANDING, which is the ratio a real character has; six of six would mean every air button gave a full ground combo.
the_six_six_six_pass.the_number_that_moved_and_why_it_moved_t: 41 simple cycles in the usable graph became 121, and 143 in the authored graph became 615. The mechanism is narrow and worth stating exactly, because 121 is not 41 plus a bit. Every cycle still leaves the air by an air_mp landing link -- air_mp is still the only move that both descends and can be re-entered -- but there are now three ways back UP into it instead of one: the launchers jump cancel into air_lp and air_lk as well as air_mp, and both lights chain into air_mp. So each of the 40 old cycles that passes through a launcher gained exactly two variants, one per air light: 8 x 2 = 16 new cycles of length 4 and 32 x 2 = 64 of length 5. 41 + 16 + 64 = 121, and the self-loop and the eight length-3 cycles are untouched.
the_six_six_six_pass.what_it_deliberately_did_not_do: RAISE THE JUGGLE BUDGET. 4 was already exactly the price of the longest air string the character can perform, and adding the lights made that string three moves long at the same price rather than more expensive: light (1) + medium (1) + heavy (2) = 4. The budget is also not what makes the character finite -- see resources[juggle].engine.semantics -- so raising it to 6 would have been a pure design change with no effect on the verdict or the certificate, and it was not needed.
the_six_six_six_pass.the_one_decision_to_re_open_first: air_hp having NO incoming cancel edge. It is what keeps the graph at 121 rather than 2905, and the measured alternative is written down in moves[air_hp].engine.role_note rather than left for somebody to rediscover. It is a clarity and tractability argument and NOT a soundness one: the verdict survives the alternative, but the authored graph would hold 9807 simple cycles, which is past the kMaxCycles of 4096 in tests/test_gap_extent.cpp, so the enumerator would stop early and the test would fail as a blown cap rather than as a moved number.

EVERY ONE OF THOSE CARRIED A NUMBER OR A LIST THAT THE FOUR NEW MOVES FALSIFIED, and this file's whole value is that its prose is checkable, so a stale sentence here is worse than no sentence.

law_1.statement: Every GROUND move is at most +2 on hit. The fastest move in the file is 3 frames. Therefore no ground move links into any ground move.
law_1.why: A link edge is a CONSEQUENCE OF FRAME DATA, not an entry in a cancel table. Any move that is +N on hit links into every move with startup <= N whether or not anybody authored it. A character whose cancel table omits those edges is a character whose model is missing edges, and missing edges is the direction that HIDES infinites. Law 1 removes the whole class instead of trying to enumerate it: with max on-hit +2 and min startup 3, the set of implied link edges is empty and THE CANCEL TABLE IS COMPLETE.
law_1.measured_against_the_corpus: This is precisely what the three transcribed characters lack. Kung Fu Girl's stand_lp is +4 with 3f startup and Kung Fu Man's is +5; ADR-001:420-432 reports both corner infinites as stand_lp into itself, authored in the .cmd as a self-chain, and confirms them line by line against the .cns rather than dismissing them as transcription bugs.
law_1.the_margin_is_one_frame_and_it_is_delibe: crouch_lp is +2 against its own 3f startup and stand_hp is +2 against the same 3 frames. Both are dead by exactly one. The two link probes in the cancels array exist so the prover PRINTS 'short by 1' rather than this file asserting it. RAISING ANY GROUND MOVE'S HITSTUN BY ONE FRAME, OR LOWERING ANY RECOVERY BY ONE, MAKES THIS CHARACTER INFINITE. That is the number not to touch, and it is the honest cost of proving termination in the corner with no hitstun decay.
law_1.what_it_costs_the_character: There are no links in the ground game, so every combo is a chain or a cancel. That is a real genre position -- it is how Darkstalkers, Marvel and Guilty Gear build combos -- but it is NOT the Street Fighter reading of an all-rounder, where a +5 medium linking into a 3f jab is the basic vocabulary. This is the one place where the ranking certificate and the genre default genuinely pull against each other, and this file resolves it toward the chain game. A link-based character can still be TERMINATING; what it cannot easily be is COMPLETE, because its real edge set is larger than its authored one.

law_2.statement: EXACTLY TWO moves are exempt from Law 1, air_mp and air_hp. Both are +7 on hit and all nine link edges each one's frame data implies are authored.
law_2.why: A jump-in that combos into a light is the most standard sequence in the genre and a character without one is not an all-rounder. The eighteen edges are authored rather than omitted precisely because Law 1's value is completeness: an exemption that hid its edges would give back everything Law 1 buys.
law_2.the_nine: air_mp links into all four lights, all four mediums, and special_uppercut. Two of them (stand_mk and crouch_mk, both 7f) are exact 1-frame links at +7.
law_2.the_second_nine: air_hp is +7 on the same arithmetic and owes the SAME nine targets, so the exemption doubled in size without changing shape. It is +7 and not more deliberately: +8 would reach crouch_hp and +11 would reach stand_hk, and a jump-in that links straight into a launcher enters the juggle loop without paying the ground combo for it.
law_2.why_the_exemption_did_not_grow_to_six: THE 6/6/6 PASS ADDED FOUR AERIALS AND ONLY ONE EXEMPTION, and the reason is the sentence Law 1 opens with -- a link edge is a consequence of FRAME DATA, not an entry in a cancel table. air_lp, air_lk and air_mk are +2 against a 3f floor, so they imply no link, need no exemption and author no landing link. That is what `air-to-air` means expressed as arithmetic rather than as a label. An earlier draft gave air_mk +5, intending a crossup that converts into a light but not into a medium; at +5 it silently owed five descending edges it did not carry, which is precisely the incompleteness Law 1 exists to prevent, and the hitstun was lowered rather than the edges added. See moves[air_mk].engine.derivation.
law_2.the_air_lights_are_law_1_compliant_by_ch: Law 1 binds GROUND moves and air_lp and air_lk obey it anyway. An air-to-air light that converted into a full ground combo would be the strongest move in the character by a distance; what they get instead is the air chain, which rewards them for hitting the opponent they were designed to hit -- an airborne one. The margin is one frame and it is PRINTED rather than asserted: the cancels array authors air_lp > stand_lp as a link probe, reported DEAD, short by 1.

law_3.statement: Juggle is spent and never gained, and every edge whose TARGET is an air move spends it. Every cycle in the usable cancel graph therefore strictly decreases juggle.
law_3.why: Law 2 puts descending edges back into the graph, so the graph has cycles again. Law 3 is what pays for them. It is the classic fix the genre already uses: a launcher into air juggles is where infinites live, and a juggle counter that only decreases is how every real game bounds them.
law_3.how_it_is_enforced: comboprover.hpp:282-290 totalEffect adds the TARGET MOVE's effect to the edge's, so charging effect.juggle -1 on air_mp itself charges every edge that enters it -- the two jump cancels and the self-cancel -- with no per-edge effect needed. nonNegative() at :264-269 then refuses the transition when the budget is gone.

termination_argument.claim: TERMINATING at stage corner, WITH a ranking certificate, and the certificate's order is [meter, juggle].
termination_argument.the_structural_proof: Order the moves L0 lights < L1 mediums < L2 heavies < L3 specials and air normals < L4 super. Every ground cancel in this file strictly ascends that order, so no cycle can be built from ground edges alone. The only descending edges in the whole graph are the eighteen landing links, air_mp's nine and air_hp's nine. To use one and return to an air move, a path must take an edge whose TARGET is an air move, and all fifteen such edges carry a negative totalEffect.juggle, because every one of the six air moves authors a negative effect.juggle and comboprover.hpp:282-290 adds the target move's effect to the edge's. Therefore every cycle strictly decreases juggle, juggle has floor 0, and no cycle can repeat unboundedly. NOTHING IN THAT ARGUMENT COUNTS AERIALS, which is why tripling the air roster did not touch it.
termination_argument.verified_by_enumeration_not_asserted: The usable cancel graph contains exactly 121 simple cycles: one of length 1 (air_mp into itself), eight of length 3, forty-eight of length 4 and sixty-four of length 5. All 121 contain at least one juggle-spending edge and NONE touches meter. The count is 41 x 3 minus 2 and that is a coincidence of arithmetic rather than a structure; the structure is this. Every cycle still leaves the air by an air_mp landing link, because air_mp remains the only move that both descends and can be re-entered. What the pass added is a second way back UP: the two launchers now jump cancel into air_lp and air_lk as well as air_mp, and both air lights chain into air_mp. So each of the 41 old cycles that passed through a launcher gained two variants -- one per air light -- which is 8 x 2 = 16 new length-4 cycles and 32 x 2 = 64 new length-5 cycles, and 41 + 16 + 64 = 121. The self-loop is unchanged, the eight length-3 cycles are unchanged, and the thirty-two old length-4 cycles are unchanged.
termination_argument.two_of_the_four_new_aerials_are_on_no_cy: MEASURED, and it is the cleanest statement of what the pass did to the graph. air_hp appears in ZERO of the 121 because nothing cancels into it -- it is a combo opener reached by jumping, and a cycle needs an incoming edge (see moves[air_hp].engine.role_note, which is where that decision is argued and where the rejected alternative is measured at 2905 cycles). air_mk appears in zero because its only outgoing edge goes to air_hk, which has none. So the two aerials that carry the most damage in the file are provably incapable of participating in a loop, and the four that can loop are the two lights, air_mp and the launchers they hang off.
termination_argument.the_juggle_economy: 4 points, six spenders, and the budget deliberately NOT raised. The longest ascending air string is light -> medium -> heavy at 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, so the budget buys exactly one complete string: air_lp > air_mp > air_hk, or air_lp > air_mk > air_hk, and nothing longer. Opening with air_hp costs 2 and leaves a light and a medium but no ender. THE BUDGET IS STILL NOT WHAT MAKES THE CHARACTER FINITE -- resources[juggle].engine.semantics records that setting it to 0 or to 40 leaves the verdict and the certificate unchanged, and that is as true with six aerials as with two, because it is the MONOTONE DECREASE that terminates the search and not the starting value. Raising it to 6 would be a pure design change: longer juggles, a slower prover search, the same verdict and the same certificate.
termination_argument.why_the_certificate_exists_here_and_nowh: comboprover.hpp:376-386 clears spendOnly if ANY reachable cancel has a positive resource effect, and :563 gates the certificate on spendOnly. ADR-001 gate 3 measured hasRanking false in 2 of 2 terminating cases for two different reasons: Kung Fu Man builds meter on hit, and AOF2 has zero usable cancels so :578-583's `if (!anyEdge) break` fires immediately. This character avoids both. It has 88 usable cancels, so anyEdge is true. And no [P] effect anywhere in the file is positive, so spendOnly survives -- the four aerials added by the 6/6/6 pass author effect.juggle -1 or -2 and nothing else, so they can only reinforce spendOnly and could never clear it.

meter_is_not_load_bearing.the_worry: Meter gain on hit is real and this file keeps it out of [P] effect to preserve spendOnly. Dropping a resource the attacker really gains UNDER-credits the attacker, and under-crediting is the direction that can HIDE an infinite (ADR-001:224-225, and the same failure the meter_room design was rejected for at :369-374). An unjustified omission here would be a soundness bug dressed as a proof.
meter_is_not_load_bearing.why_it_cannot_hide_a_loop_in_THIS_charac: super_beam is the only move in the file that spends meter, and super_beam has ZERO outgoing cancels. Meter therefore appears on no cycle at all: it gates exactly one class of terminal edge. The set of cycles in this graph is independent of the meter value, so no amount of meter, gained or not, can create a loop that the model does not already see.
meter_is_not_load_bearing.the_counterfactual_that_checks_it: Set resources[meter].initial to 0, or to 100000, or delete super_beam's effect and guard entirely, and re-analyse. The verdict must stay TERMINATING and the usable/dead split must stay 88/6 in all three cases. If any of them changes, this argument is wrong and the meter gain must go back into [P] effect at the cost of the certificate.
meter_is_not_load_bearing.what_it_would_cost_to_be_honest_the_othe: Authoring stand_lp effect.meter +4 -- this character's real gain, and one unit less than Kung Fu Girl's +5 -- leaves the verdict TERMINATING and turns spendOnly false, hasRanking false, rankingOrder empty. That is the ordinary result ADR-001 gate 3 describes, and it is one keystroke away in either direction. The certificate is bought by exactly this decision and by nothing else.

termination_argument.what_the_certificate_does_and_does_not_s: READ THE TOOL CAREFULLY HERE. comboprover.hpp:563-613 builds the order greedily: it takes a resource that decreases on some live edge and increases on none, records it, DELETES every edge that decreases it, and repeats. hasRanking is set from `!rankingOrder.empty()` at :612, so it becomes true as soon as ONE resource is extracted -- it does not mean the ranking function explains the whole graph. On this character the loop extracts meter (killing the 6 super edges), then juggle (killing the 15 edges into air moves), and then stops with 67 live edges still standing: 32 chains, 17 special cancels and 18 landing links, none of which touches a resource. Those 67 are not covered by the certificate. They are acyclic, and it is the DFS at :469-539 that proved it, not the ranking function. So the true statement is: the lexicographic order (meter, juggle) strictly decreases on every edge that spends anything, and the edges it does not cover form an acyclic subgraph. describe() at :708-714 prints 'ends because these run down, in order: meter, juggle', which is a fair summary of the first half and silent about the second.
termination_argument.midscreen: Not the question this file is posed for, and expected TERMINATING as well: stage midscreen adds a synthesized __space resource and reach guards, which can only remove edges from a graph whose sole cycle class is already juggle-bounded. Note that the certificate is a CORNER concept regardless -- hasRanking is computed by the C++ header, which does not implement midscreen at all (:15-24), and midscreen's walking gap action gives __space back, which would clear spendOnly in the Python model.

chain.authored_as: A strictly ascending magic series: lights chain to mediums, mediums chain to heavies, nothing chains within a tier or downward. The ascending restriction is not decoration -- an intra-tier chain such as stand_lp -> crouch_lp is a 2-cycle with no resource cost, which is an infinite.
chain.delay_rule: 2 on every edge. Each move's engine.cancel_window_ticks opens at startup + 2, and delay = window open - startup.
chain.caveat: 2 is the smallest delay this file authors and it is authored rather than defaulted. ADR-001:434-442 calls the discovery that MUGEN chain cancels are NOT delay 0 the hardest single finding of Phase 0.

special_cancel.authored_as: The light punches, all four mediums and stand_hp cancel into fireball and uppercut; the mediums and stand_hp also cancel into dash_punch. The light KICKS do not special-cancel, which is why they have 4 outgoing edges and the light punches have 6.
special_cancel.delay_rule: 3. One tick later than a chain, because a special needs a motion input to complete.
special_cancel.caveat: The two light -> fireball edges are DEAD by 4 frames and are authored anyway, because 'your jab does not combo into your fireball' is exactly the thing the editor panel exists to tell a designer. It is also the correct genre answer.

super_cancel.authored_as: crouch_mk, stand_hp and crouch_hp super-cancel directly; all three specials super-cancel.
super_cancel.delay_rule: 4. Two ticks later than a chain, because the super needs a double motion.

super_cancel_projectile.delay_rule: 3, NOT 4, and the difference is the schema's prescribed soundness fix rather than an inconsistency. See moves[special_fireball].engine.projectile_prover_note.

jump_cancel.authored_as: stand_hk and crouch_hp only. These are the only two moves whose 30 and 27 frames of hitstun are reachable by anything, and only through this window. EACH NOW REACHES FOUR AERIALS RATHER THAN ONE: air_lp, air_lk, air_mp and air_mk, which is every air move fast enough to catch a rising opponent.
jump_cancel.delay_rule: 5: four pre-jump ticks plus one tick of transition.
jump_cancel.the_rule_about_which_aerials: NO AIR HEAVY IS A JUMP-CANCEL TARGET. The file has always had this rule and used to have one instance of it -- air_hk was never jump-cancellable into -- and the 6/6/6 pass made it a rule with two, by declining to author a launcher into air_hp as well. The reason is the same for both: a launched opponent is rising, and a 9f or 8f aerial arrives after they are out of reach. IT IS A DESIGN RESTRICTION AND NOT AN ARITHMETIC ONE, which is worth stating because the frame data would happily permit it -- stand_hk leaves 30 - 5 = 25 of advantage against air_hp's 8f startup. It is also the decision that keeps the cycle count at 121; see moves[air_hp].engine.role_note for the measured alternative.

air_chain.authored_as: The two air lights into the two air mediums: air_lp and air_lk each into air_mp and air_mk. Four edges, added by the 6/6/6 pass, and the reason the air lights are worth having.
air_chain.delay_rule: 2 on every edge, the SAME rule and the same number as a ground chain: each move's engine.cancel_window_ticks opens at startup + 2, and delay = window open - startup.
air_chain.caveat: THE AIR TWIN OF `chain`, ascending exactly one tier. There is no light-to-heavy chain on the ground and there is none in the air; reaching an air HEAVY costs the air action instead and belongs to juggle_cancel at delay 5. That split is what makes an air string at most three moves long, and it is also what makes the budget of 4 buy exactly one of them. THE STRICTLY ASCENDING RESTRICTION IS NOT DECORATION HERE ANY MORE THAN IT IS ON THE GROUND: an intra-tier air chain such as air_lp -> air_lk would be a 2-cycle, and although juggle would still bound it -- every air move spends -- it would be a loop the character does not mean to have.

juggle_cancel.authored_as: air_mp into air_mp and into air_hk, and air_mk into air_hk, using the character's one air action.
juggle_cancel.delay_rule: 5, the same air-action cost as a jump cancel.
juggle_cancel.caveat: air_mp -> air_mp is STILL the ONLY self-loop in the usable graph -- the 6/6/6 pass deliberately added none, because a second self-loop would have multiplied the length-1 cycles for no design gain -- and it is the reason this character needs a resource argument at all. Delete effect.juggle from air_mp and the verdict is INFINITE with the loop printed as air_mp. The third edge, air_mk -> air_hk, gives the air-to-air medium the same terminator air_mp has, so BOTH air mediums end the string in the knockdown and neither ends it in air_hp.

landing_link.condition: self.move_hit, then the attacker waits out landing recovery
landing_link.authored_as: air_mp into all four lights, all four mediums and special_uppercut at delay 15, and air_hp into the same nine at delay 21: the eighteen edges Law 2 owes.
landing_link.delay_rule: active + recovery - 1 -- 15 for air_mp and 21 for air_hp -- authored as an explicit number AND as kind: link so that a reader honouring either computes the same delay.
landing_link.why_no_air_target_appears_in_either_set: Both sources are +7, and air_lp starts in 4, so a reader may reasonably ask why neither aerial links into another aerial. Because a LANDING link starts from the floor, and reaching an air move from the floor costs the jump, which this file prices at 5 in the jump_cancel family. +7 against 4 + 5 = 9 is short by two. The rule was already implicit in air_mp's nine targets before this pass and is stated now that there are two sources to be consistent about.

link_probe.condition: none -- these edges are authored to be reported DEAD
link_probe.authored_as: special_fireball into itself, crouch_lp into itself, stand_hp into stand_lp, and air_lp into stand_lp.
link_probe.caveat: These four are not cancels the character has; they are the links its frame data implies, written down so that the prover prints its own margin. THREE of them are now short by exactly 1 and that trio IS Law 1: crouch_lp and stand_hp on the ground, and air_lp in the air since the 6/6/6 pass. The fourth answers the brief's requirement that the fireball have a real recovery: short by 24, so the fireball cannot chase its own hit. ONE PROBE COVERS BOTH AIR LIGHTS: air_lk has the identical L of 14 and the identical hitstun of 16, so it is dead by the same one frame and a second probe would print the same sentence twice.

hit_rules.summary: Two character-level rules, both authored as structured move.hit_condition on every move and both invisible to today's loader (field class E5).
hit_rules.ground_rule: A grounded normal does not connect against an airborne defender. This is the same shape as Kung Fu Girl's !var(16) && var(15) < 1 on all 17 of its normals (ADR-001:255-260), which is the largest single gap the Phase-0 transcription found by move count.
hit_rules.air_rule: An air attack needs a juggle point. Unlike the ground rule this one is ALSO expressed prover-visibly, as [P] effect.juggle plus nonNegative(), so the model enforces it rather than ignoring it.
hit_rules.the_important_property: NO EDGE IS OMITTED FROM THIS FILE ON THE STRENGTH OF A PREDICATE THE PROVER CANNOT SEE. Every edge the character lacks, it lacks because of frame data the prover CAN see. The ground rule would forbid, for instance, stand_hk -> stand_lp; but stand_hk is +2 on hit and stand_lp starts in 3, so that edge is dead on Law 1 alone and the predicate is never load-bearing. This is checkable: no ground move is more than +2, so the set of edges the predicate uniquely removes is empty.

moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.crouch_hk: The sweep. Hard knockdown, fall_recover_ticks 20. Nothing follows a knockdown in the running game, and it is -8 on hit besides, so even without the knockdown no link exists.
moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.air_hk: The juggle ender. Hard knockdown, and +2 on hit so Law 1 forbids a link independently.
moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.super_beam: The super. Its fifth hit is a hard knockdown and it is -13 on hit.
moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.note: All three are enders on TWO independent grounds -- a knockdown the prover cannot see, and frame data it can. Only the second is doing any work in the model, and that is deliberate: x-known-over-approximations.defender_has_no_state means the prover would happily continue a combo past a hit that really ends it, so a file that leaned on knockdown to terminate would be leaning on something the tool ignores.

cancel_note.dead_list: stand_lp -> special_fireball (short by 4), crouch_lp -> special_fireball (short by 4), special_fireball -> special_fireball (short by 24), crouch_lp -> crouch_lp (short by 1), stand_hp -> stand_lp (short by 1), air_lp -> stand_lp (short by 1).
cancel_note.by_family: 32 chain, 19 special_cancel (17 usable), 5 super_cancel, 1 super_cancel_projectile, 8 jump_cancel, 3 juggle_cancel, 4 air_chain, 18 landing_link, 4 link_probe (0 usable). The 6/6/6 pass added 21 edges: 6 jump_cancel, 4 air_chain, 1 juggle_cancel, 9 landing_link and 1 link_probe. IT ADDED NO EDGE OUT OF air_mp, whose eleven outgoing edges -- nine landing links and two air-to-air -- are byte-identical to what they were before.
cancel_note.on_block_edges_not_authored: Every edge in this file is on: hit. MUGEN's Movecontact means hit OR block and the prover's vocabulary has no such value (schema $defs.cancel), but this character is not a MUGEN import and the omission here is simply that the block half does not change a verdict: model.py:81 COMBO_CONTACT counts only hit and always. The block half exists in the running game -- every special cancel is available on block -- and belongs in the engine's own cancel table, not in the prover's.

engine.anim_note: Per-frame sprite references and 4 x int16 sub-unit hit/hurt/push boxes are NOT authored here. ADR-001:463-466 records that they are transcribed for none of the 59 corpus moves either, and no prover field depends on them. move.engine.reaction carries everything the hit resolver needs that the prover's single hitstun cannot hold; the boxes are the hitbox editor's job in Phase 3, and move.reach plus quantized_sources carry the one number the model reads from them.

fit.what_this_number_does_and_does_not_show: 0 of 22 against ADR-001's 23 of 59 is NOT evidence that this character is simpler than a real one. It is evidence of the direction of authoring. The Phase-0 rate measured a transcription being pushed into a schema drafted before the data was read; this one measures a character authored against the schema after it was fixed. A rate of 0 here is the expected result if ADR-001 section 4's nine fields were the right nine, and it is worth exactly that much: a NEGATIVE result -- an original character that still needed a tenth field -- would have been the informative one, and it did not occur.
schema_limits: A minimum gap is not expressible: guard is componentwise >= only, so move.reach can bound the gap from above and never from below. This character does not use a proximity pair, so the limit is untested here rather than closed.

A projectile's contact frame is a function of distance and [P] startup is a constant. Not closable by a field. This file applies the schema's prescribed mitigation -- author the outgoing delay at point-blank contact -- at the first edge in the project that needs it.
The prover has no defender state, so knockdown cannot end a combo in the model. Three moves in this file cause one; none of them relies on it.
known_losses: METER GAIN IS ABSENT FROM [P] effect while engine.reaction.meter_gain_units carries it on all 18 moves. DIRECTION: under-credits the attacker, which is the CONSERVATIVE direction and CAN HIDE AN INFINITE. This is the dangerous direction and it is the one loss in this file that needed a real argument rather than a note. The argument is structural -- super_beam is the only meter spender and has no outgoing edges, so meter is on no cycle -- and it is falsifiable by the counterfactual named in termination_argument.meter_is_not_load_bearing. It is also mitigated by starting meter at the ceiling rather than at a typical value.

The fireball's super-cancel delay is authored from POINT-BLANK contact (3) rather than from release (4). DIRECTION: over-credits the attacker by one frame, PERMISSIVE, safe. This is deliberate and is the schema's own prescription for the projectile over-approximation.

The SEVEN on_land recoveries are LOWER bounds measured on the neutral jump arc -- three before the 6/6/6 pass and one per aerial added by it. DIRECTION: PERMISSIVE, safe. It matters most on air_mp and air_hp, whose recoveries set the two +7s that Law 2 depends on, and it matters newly on air_lp, air_lk and air_mk in the OPPOSITE way: their +2 is what keeps them Law 1 compliant, and a recovery that is a lower bound means the real advantage can only be SMALLER than +2, never larger. So the bound cannot turn an air light into a converting overhead by accident.

move.hit_condition and move.stance are invisible to the fragment: json_spec.py never reads hit_condition, and comboprover.hpp's Move has no stance field at all. DIRECTION: PERMISSIVE, safe. Measured to be INERT in this file -- see hit_rules.the_important_property -- because no edge is omitted on their strength.

SCHEMA v3'S FOUR FIELDS ARE DATA AND NOT YET BEHAVIOUR, and the gap is wide enough to state plainly rather than let a reader assume the annotation did something. move.stance is reported by MatchBuilder as a KernelPermits loss over all 18 moves because the kernel gates starting a move on hitstun and blockstun only -- a `crouching` move remains startable in the air, and v3 makes the field precise without making it enforced. blocked_as is further back than that: cse::kernel::Combat.h scopes blocking out entirely (`Fighter::blockstun exists and nothing ever writes it`), so there is nothing yet for a guard height to be checked against. engine.hurtbox_sub closes only the DEFENDER's half of low-profiling -- the schema still authors no vertical extent for an ATTACK, so every hitbox spans the whole body and a shorter crouch is data nothing consumes. engine.airborne_from_tick has no consumer at all. DIRECTION: none, because none of the four is read by anything that decides anything. Authoring the data before the rules is the right order (ADR-006 section 10 item 6): the alternative is a kernel rule with no file able to describe the character it applies to.
Knockdown ends three moves in the running game and the prover cannot see it. DIRECTION: PERMISSIVE, safe, and inert because all three moves have zero outgoing edges anyway.

Blockstun exists on every move as engine data and has no [P] home, so the on-block column of this character's frame chart is invisible to the prover. It cannot move a verdict: only hit and always continue a combo.

NOT A LOSS, recorded because a reader will look for one here: the juggle reset. It happens when the combo ends, which is outside the cancel graph by construction, so modelling juggle as monotone within a combo is EXACT.

measured.status: NOT MEASURED IN THIS FILE. ADR-001's fit.measured is required to come from an actual `python -m comboprover analyse` run and to be re-measured rather than predicted, and this file is authored ahead of that run. The author's PREDICTION -- corner: TERMINATING, spend-only fragment, 88 usable / 6 dead, hasRanking true with rankingOrder [meter, juggle], 121 simple cycles in the usable graph and 615 in the authored one -- is recorded in termination_argument as a claim to be checked, not as a result. If the run disagrees, the run is right.
measured.what_the_6_6_6_pass_predicts_will_MOVE: STATED AHEAD OF THE RUN so a deliberate change can be told from a regression. tests/test_gap_extent.cpp asserts 143 authored / 41 usable cycles with a 1/8/32 length split, 68 usable and 5 dead cancels, 41 ended by juggle, 1 fully takeable, 40 empty-windowed, 33 unescapable and 8 escapable. The new values are 615 / 121 with a 1/8/48/64 split, 88 usable and 6 dead, 121 ended by juggle, 1 fully takeable, 120 empty-windowed, and a PREDICTED 97 unescapable against 24 escapable. THREE OF THAT FILE'S static_asserts ENCODE COINCIDENCES OF A TWO-AERIAL CHARACTER AND WILL FAIL TO COMPILE RATHER THAN FAIL AT RUNTIME: `kEmptyWindowed == kLengthThree + kLengthFour` should be `kUsableCycles - kSelfLoops`; `kEscapable == kLengthThree` should be `the cycles whose landing link enters a medium`, which is now the 8 of length 3 plus 16 of length 4; and `kUnescapable == kByCancelAlone + kByHeldButton` needs its two terms re-measured. The escapable figure of 24 is the one number here that is a MODEL of a simulation rather than an enumeration, and it is the one to trust least: it assumes the leak is decided solely by whether air_mp's landing link enters a light or a medium, which is the mechanism that file measures, applied to 80 more cycles than it measured it on.
